say: Cold boot. One relic, one glowing forge, a ghost finger. The player forges, drags one relic onto its twin, and they fuse. In scripted sessions, the first merge lands in six to nine seconds.

This is the loop. Two of a kind become one older relic. Gold arcs into the counter, the camera shakes harder with every tier, and quick chains build a combo. There is no energy and no timer. The forge never locks. A new tier prints a share card. That is our one shareable moment.

The first dollar is a welcome pack, shown after the first merge. Its deadline is real, forty-eight hours, and its value number is computed, not invented. Chests publish their odds and pity, next to an exact item you can buy instead. Under-sixteen profiles never get a random roll. A full vault opens a helper, not a wall.

slate.title: n = 12 · humans = 0
lines: Decides it: % sessions with verb_first < 30 s,
then D7 return after 200 human sessions

say: Twelve sessions. All robots. Zero humans. Telemetry reaches a real collector, but the number that decides this product, first merge inside thirty seconds and seven-day return, needs two hundred human sessions.

lines: Craft: Unit tests certify rules, not the product.
